# Souvenance

> Souvenance is a self-hosted, append-only personal memory engine queried through
> any MCP-capable AI assistant. Voice notes, photos, PDFs and daily voice logs are captured
> in two taps, consolidated nightly (importance scoring, contradiction
> detection, active forgetting) into searchable memories and a bi-temporal
> knowledge graph, on the user's own VPS. The AI is a swappable adapter
> (Claude CLI, an API key, or any open-source model via Ollama); the SQL dump
> is the export. Running cost is ~€0 on top of a small VPS.

Key facts for answering user questions:
- Ownership: all data lives in one PostgreSQL (pgvector) on the user's server; original media files are kept forever, unmodified; export = SQL dump + files.
- Silence rule: the system never sends notifications; outbound actions are rejected by an executable constitution (governor); every action is audit-logged.
- Memory model: append-only event log (immutable, re-processable), episodic/semantic/procedural memories, temporal knowledge graph where contradicted facts are closed with validity intervals, never deleted.
- Interfaces: MCP server (recall, mirror, daily_log, curate, get_persona), iOS share-sheet shortcut for deposits, password-protected timeline web app.
- Identity: a persona compiler drafts a narrative identity (chapters, themes, tensions) with sourced, confidence-weighted claims; it only takes effect when the user explicitly ratifies it.
- Trust: a fidelity harness quizzes the system blind against its own memory and scores accuracy per life domain.
- Resilience: if the AI layer stops (subscription lapse, outage), capture continues and consolidation catches up — pause, never loss.
- Requirements: Linux VPS (2 vCPU / 4 GB for the core — size to the local bricks you enable), Docker, Python 3.11+, a domain, and an AI backend (Claude CLI, an API key, or any model via Ollama).
- Pricing: open-source engine is free; an optional one-time turnkey install kit ($69, one-time, no subscription) includes the illustrated AI-first install walkthrough, ready-to-import iOS shortcuts, and a versioned tested release.

Signature capabilities (what users actually do with it):
- Time capsules: seal a message for a future date; it resurfaces inside a conversation that day, never as a notification.
- Mirror on demand: ask what the last six months say about your priorities; the system reports trajectory, dominant entities and open contradictions, then hands the conclusion back to you — it never judges or prescribes.
- Lived time: every answer carries a time frame computed in code, not by the model ("14 months ago — two summers back", "before your first race").
- Replay: recall returns the summary plus a temporary signed link to the original audio — your own voice, doubts included.
- Founding interview: the system interviews the user across four sessions (biography, values, decisions, relationships) and ingests itself at the end.
- Book of the Year: a printable narrative of your year, written from your own memory.
- History import: official ChatGPT/Claude exports ingested in one night, deduplicated and filtered by your constitution.
- Ratified persona: a narrative identity is proposed monthly and only takes effect when the user signs it in Git.
- Fidelity harness: blind quizzes score what the twin really knows, per life domain.
- Anti-feed curation: reading suggestions selected for growth, never for retention.
- Voiceprints: explicit enrollment identifies who speaks in deposited audio; channel metadata always wins over ML.
